noAccess.body: Your role does not include the KPI library. Ask the owner or an administrator if you need it.

error.read: The server did not answer as expected. Try again in a moment.
error.forbidden: Your role does not allow this.

problem.MIXED_CURRENCIES: Money in several currencies without a rate

status.differs: Names other facts than its calculation

library.title: Every KPI
library.intro: One place for every KPI, so a number means the same everywhere: what it means in plain words, who owns it, its value now for what you may see, its version and what reads it.
library.failed: The KPI library could not be read
library.noMatchBody: Try other words, or show every area.
library.stale: The list may be out of date
library.foot: Values are read from the metric layer, rebuilt every hour; a value older than 3 hours says so. Targets per site come later.

held.nothingToExport: No KPI is shown to export.
held.ownerOnly: Changing a KPI is the owner’s (KPI library: manage).
held.notInstalled: Install the standard KPIs first: a new version starts from the one in force.
held.draftWaiting: Draft version {version} is waiting: edit it, put it in force or delete it first.

install.inForce: Each is written as version 1 in force, owned by its standard role, with its words in Italian and English.
install.uses: What already reads them (Today’s key numbers) is listed under Where used.
install.doneBody: They are in force: their values come with the next rebuild of the facts.
install.nothing: Every standard KPI was already installed.
install.refused: The standard KPIs were not installed
install.readerNote_one: {count} standard KPI is not installed yet: the owner installs it.
install.readerNote_other: {count} standard KPIs are not installed yet: the owner installs them.

kpi.notFoundBody: The address names a KPI the library does not have. Go back to the library to find it.
kpi.failed: The KPI could not be read
kpi.stale: This page may be out of date

calc.BALANCE: What stands at the end of the period
calc.RATIO: One sum over another, over the period

banner.notInstalledOwner: These are the standard words: installing writes them as version 1 in force, with the other standard KPIs the company lacks.
banner.notInstalledBody: These are the standard words. The owner installs the standard KPIs; until then nothing reads it.
banner.draft: Version {version} is a draft: not in force yet
banner.draftBody: Edit it, put it in force or delete it.
banner.draftReader: The owner puts it in force.
banner.differs: This version names other facts than its calculation reads
banner.differsBody: Its calculation reads: {facts}. A new version written here names exactly those, so it can be put in force.
banner.withdrawnBody: No version is in force: dashboards, reports and alerts do not read it. Its versions are kept to explain old numbers.

words.title: In words
words.periodRules: Weeks run Monday to Sunday (ISO); months, quarters and years follow the calendar; fiscal quarters and years follow each company’s fiscal year. A day is the site’s own clock, else the company’s; a shift belongs to the day it began.

now.title: Now
now.stale: The facts are more than 3 hours old: the hourly rebuild is late.
now.live: Counted live from your own records (your role reaches some customers only).
now.missingDays_one: {count} day of the period is not built yet.
now.missingDays_other: {count} days of the period are not built yet.
now.converted: Includes amounts in {currencies}, at each day’s rate.
now.noRecordsPage: The list of its records has no page yet.

uses.title: Used in
uses.intro: Every dashboard, report and alert that reads this KPI: they all read this definition and this calculation.
uses.emptyBody: Dashboards, reports and alerts that read it are listed here as soon as they do.

noPage.DASHBOARD: Its dashboard has no page yet.
noPage.REPORT: This report has no page here.
noPage.ALERT: This alert has no page here.

alert.ORDER_LATE_RISK: Orders at risk of being late
alert.MATERIAL_SHORT: Material short for a work order

history.title: Versions
history.intro: Every change to the definition, so an old number can be explained.
history.emptyBody: The standard words become version 1 when the owner installs the standard KPIs.
history.compareIntro: What one version says differently from another, field by field.
history.oneVersionBody: When a second version is written, the two compare here.
history.same: The two versions say the same.

activate.question: Put version {version} of “{name}” in force?
activate.supersedes: Version {version} is superseded: it is kept to explain old numbers.
activate.readers: Every dashboard, report and alert that reads “{name}” shows version {version}’s words from now on.

delete.question: Delete draft version {version}?
delete.gone: Draft version {version} is gone for good.
delete.kept: The versions that were in force stay, to explain old numbers.

retire.question: Withdraw “{name}”?
retire.nothing: No version is in force any more.
retire.uses_one: {count} use goes with it: what read it stops reading it.
retire.uses_other: {count} uses go with it: what read it stops reading it.
retire.kept: Version {version} is kept to explain old numbers; a new version can be written and put in force later.

install.question: Install the standard KPIs?
install.this: “{name}” is written as version 1 in force, with its standard words.
install.others: Every other standard KPI the company lacks is installed too.

done.drafted: Draft version {version} saved: put it in force when it is right.
done.retired_one: Withdrawn: version {version} is no longer in force ({count} use removed).
done.retired_other: Withdrawn: version {version} is no longer in force ({count} uses removed).

form.newIntro: It starts as a draft with the words of the version in force; put it in force when it is right. Its calculation stays the same: a different calculation is a different KPI.
form.editIntro: A draft changes until it is put in force; then it never changes again.
form.definitionHint: Say what it counts and what it leaves out.
form.ownerHint: The office role that answers for this definition.
form.ownerHeld: Choosing another owner needs the right to see roles; it stays as it is.
form.fixed: Set by its calculation: reads {facts} · counts in {unit} · needs {rights}.
form.fixesTitle: The new version names its calculation’s facts
form.fixesBody: The version it starts from names other facts; this one names exactly what its calculation reads, so it can be put in force.
form.changeNoteHint: It stays in the history, so an old number can be explained.
form.nothingChanged: Nothing changed from the version in force: change a word, the records or the owner first.

problem.nameIt: The name is 1 to {name} characters on one line.
problem.nameEn: The name is 1 to {name} characters on one line.
problem.definitionIt: Say what it means in 1 to {definition} characters.
problem.definitionEn: Say what it means in 1 to {definition} characters.
problem.formulaIt: Give the formula in 1 to {formula} characters.
problem.formulaEn: Give the formula in 1 to {formula} characters.
problem.sourceRecords: Name 1 to {records} records, each once, by their record name.
problem.ownerRoleId: Choose an office role that is not archived.
problem.changeNote: Say what changed, in 1 to {note} characters.

refusal.UNKNOWN_MEASURE: It reads a fact the metric layer does not build yet: it cannot be put in force.
refusal.MEASURES_DIFFER: The version names other facts than its calculation reads: write a new version, which names them exactly.
refusal.UNIT_DIFFERS: The version counts in another unit than its calculation.
refusal.GRAIN_DIFFERS: The version asks other money rights than its calculation.
refusal.NOT_DRAFT: Only a draft changes or is deleted: this version is no longer a draft.
refusal.NOT_IN_FORCE: No version is in force any more: someone withdrew it meanwhile.
refusal.BASED_ON_OTHER_KPI: A new version starts from a version of the same KPI.
refusal.IN_FORCE: This version is in force: it is never changed. Write a new version from it.
refusal.ENDED: This version is no longer in force: it is kept as it was, to explain old numbers.
refusal.KEPT: This version was in force: it explains old numbers and is never deleted. Only a draft is deleted.
refusal.STATE: A version is written as a draft, then put in force, then superseded or withdrawn; it never goes back.
refusal.FACTS: The figures of a day could not be written: rebuild them again.
refusal.stale: Someone changed this KPI meanwhile: the page reads it again; try once more.
refusal.forbidden: Your role does not allow this (KPI library: manage).
refusal.stepUp: This step asks for a fresh authenticator code.
refusal.gone: This version is gone: someone deleted it meanwhile.
refusal.offline: The server cannot be reached: nothing was changed.
refusal.invalid: The server refused what was sent as it is.
refusal.failed: It did not work. Nothing was changed; try again.

note.materialsShort_other: {count} materials short for open work orders.
